To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean incoming wind velocity measured with a nacelle sonic is higher than that of SLPIV due to the induction effect and the nacelle blockage effect.

SLPIV measurements of a utility-scale wind turbine can be used to characterize incoming flow and the discrepancy of the velocity measured by nacelle sonic is affected by yaw error, incident angle, and short term fluctuations of the incoming wind.

SLPIV measurements of incoming wind velocity at 85 m upstream of a 2 MW wind turbine rotor show that the induction zone is steeper and more confined than predicted by vortex theory, that the mean velocity measured at the nacelle by a sonic anemometer is generally matched with SLPIV measured velocity outside the induction, that the velocity ratio between the sonic anemometer at the naceller and the SLPIV velocity outside induction is normally distributed and less than unity 90%
In summary, our research is concerned with
the incoming flow characterization of the 2.5MW wind turbine at high spatial and temporal resolution, using SLPIV, a novel technique for wind energy research.
the characterization of the wind field in the vicinity of a utility scale turbine using super large-scale particle image velocimetric measurements.
the incoming flow of a utility scale turbine.

yaw error has the strongest effect on the discrepancy, followed by the incident angle and the short term intensity of velocity fluctuation.
the SLPIV velocity measurements can be used to validate sonic anemometer measurements, but with the understanding of its limitations.
the sonic anemometer measures the velocity in the rotor plane with an uncertainty that depends on the yaw error and the incident angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SLPIV is a promising method for characterizing the incoming wind flow to wind turbines and can be used as a validation tool for CFD simulations.
the incoming flow of a utility scale turbine is characterized by a distinct region of enhanced vertical velocity.
, SLPIV measurements of the incoming wind flow to wind turbines are feasible and have potential in improving our understanding of the wind flow around the rotor plane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sonic anemometer is a valid measurement of incoming wind velocity, and can be used to validate CFD and LES models.
the sonic anemometer measurements are a good approximation of the SLPIV measurements outside the induction zone.
super large scale particle velocimetry can be used to characterize wind turbines in the field.
